auxiliary_material.content: Used a linear mixed-effect model (LMM) to analyze longitudinal metabolite data across 7 time points up to 12 months post-surgery.
auxiliary_material.relevance: Methodological reference for handling unbalanced longitudinal metabolomics data in clinical studies, useful for designing future serum/TME monitoring studies.

auxiliary_material.content: Incurred sample reanalysis (ISR) confirmed method robustness over time (15 samples reanalyzed, meeting EMA criteria of <20% difference in 67% of repeats).
auxiliary_material.relevance: Supports the importance of ISR in validating long-term metabolite quantification stability, a criterion relevant for establishing standardized methods in any matrix.

outline_action: Search specifically for validated LC-MS/MS or NMR protocols for inosine and SCFAs in serum or tissue samples. Look for consensus statements from metabolomics societies (e.g., MSI) regarding absolute quantification standards in blood/tissue. Compare urine-based validation parameters with existing serum method requirements to identify matrix-specific gaps (e.g., protein interference, stability).
remaining_gap: This study validates inosine quantification in urine, not serum or tumor microenvironment (TME). It does not address short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) at all. No consensus guidelines for absolute concentration measurement of inosine or SCFAs specifically in serum/TME were identified in this text. The physiological concentration ranges provided are urine-specific (creatinine-normalized) and cannot be directly extrapolated to serum/TME standards.

useful_material.content: Developed and validated a targeted LC-MS/MS method for absolute quantification of inosine in human urine, following FDA and EMA bioanalytical guidelines (linearity, accuracy, precision, LOQ, stability).
useful_material.relevance: Demonstrates a rigorous standardized workflow for inosine quantification, providing methodological parameters (e.g., LOQ 0.040 µM, linearity 0.05–5 µM) that can inform serum/TME method development, though the matrix differs.

useful_material.content: Reported absolute concentration ranges of inosine in bladder cancer patients before and after tumor resection (e.g., 0.16 ± 0.12 µM/mM creatinine pre-surgery), normalized to creatinine.
useful_material.relevance: Provides empirical data on inosine physiological levels in a cancer context, supporting the feasibility of detecting inosine changes associated with tumor burden, even if urine levels do not directly equate to serum/TME concentrations.

useful_material.content: Sample preparation involved simple protein precipitation (methanol:water 1:1) and centrifugation without solid-phase extraction.
useful_material.relevance: Offers a simplified protocol example for nucleoside extraction that could be adapted for serum processing, reducing complexity compared to SPE methods.
